reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only confirms that oxidative wear occurs alongside abrasive and adhesive wear in HEA alloys, but does not demonstrate that a continuous nanocrystalline oxide glaze forms in-situ as a protective barrier or that it is the primary governor of wear resistance. E3 discusses friction coefficient changes with composition but does not address oxide layer formation or oxygen availability. Thus, the key premises about the specific protective mechanism and its controlling role are unsupported.
premises: Friction-induced heating and stress in HEA coatings promote in-situ oxide layer formation
The oxide layer is continuous and nanocrystalline, acting as a mechanical barrier
This oxide layer reduces direct metal contact and localizes shear, mitigating abrasive and adhesive wear
Oxygen availability controls oxide layer formation and thus wear performance
The mechanism is active up to ~800 °C where oxidation kinetics are sufficient
